title: Departure Manifest and Pilgrim Operations
outcome: Approved operator staff can open a departure-level pilgrim manifest, see each traveller's operational readiness and blockers across booking, payments, documents, visa and accommodation, record governed readiness actions and prepare a reliable handoff without mutating source-module state.
actor: Approved operator staff responsible for pre-departure pilgrim operations.
modules: Booking owns the departure-manifest operational projection, operator notes/readiness decisions, concurrency versions and append-only readiness audit history.
Payments, Documents, Visa and Accommodation remain authoritative for their own status and are read through explicit module contracts or existing projections; VS-27 does not mutate their tables.
Catalogue/Departure data remains authoritative for departure identity and schedule.
Web adds a departure-level Pilgrim manifest workspace using the established NoorPath operator shell and visual language.
routes: Manifest -> search/filter travellers and review blockers
Manifest -> review departure counts and audit history
acceptance: Only an approved operator can read or mutate manifest operations for departures owned by the active operator; foreign ids return safe not-found responses.
The manifest consolidates confirmed-booking travellers for the selected departure and exposes departure-level totals for total, ready and blocked travellers.
Each traveller row exposes explicit readiness indicators for payment, documents, visa and accommodation using authoritative source-module state without cross-module mutations.
A traveller is not operationally ready while any required readiness indicator is blocked or incomplete; the UI identifies the blocking reason rather than relying on colour alone.
Search and filters work across traveller name, booking reference and readiness state without hiding blocked travellers by default.
Operator readiness actions and notes require an explicit reason/note, current version and actor context; stale writes fail with conflict feedback and no partial mutation.
Every governed readiness action records actor account, operator, traveller/departure scope, before/after state, reason, correlation id and timestamp in append-only audit history.
Manifest operations do not change booking price, payment history, document state, visa state, room assignments or cancellation state.
The workspace includes loading, empty, error, permission, stale/conflict and retry states and remains keyboard-operable and usable at approved desktop/mobile viewports.
Desktop and mobile navigation, target size, reflow and serious/critical accessibility checks pass.
Product Owner approval is required for the exact certified SHA before merge; production deployment remains separately approved.
policyDecisionsRequired: Treat readiness as an operational projection derived from authoritative module state rather than a replacement domain state.
Do not allow manual readiness to override hard blockers from payments, documents, visa or accommodation; operator actions may add notes/acknowledgement only where source state is complete.
Use optimistic versions for readiness notes/actions so concurrent operators cannot silently overwrite operational decisions.
Keep readiness audit history append-only with actor, reason and correlation metadata.
exclusions: Payment capture, adjustment or refund execution.
